q-111623.name: Question 1
q-111623.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218944/assets/869e65cb2894403a5fe9f5e5f68e1c7882f8c86aff7596e557958e1f6cbbe348.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=f(3x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-111623.worked_solution:
To graph the function $y=f(3x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and compress it by factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218944/assets/b84a3ca0b17949c07748e73235d026d696c199136e448b32639959036c5389a8.png)

q-249484.name: Question 5
q-249484.problem:
The point $P$ with coordinates $(2,-5)$ lies on the curve $y=f(7x).$ Find the point $Q$ that must lie on $y=f(x).$

The coordinates of $Q$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
q-249484.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(\frac{1}{7}\cdot (7x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(7x)$ by a factor of $7$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(7x)$ by $7.$

Therefore, the point $(2,-5)$ on $f(7x)$ is mapped to the point $(7\cdot 2,-5)=(14,-5),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$

−5

q-112072.name: Question 7
q-112072.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(18,-12)$ lies on the curve $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
q-112072.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(6\cdot (\frac{1}{6}x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a compression of the function $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ by a factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ by $6.$

Therefore, the point $(18,-12)$ on $f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ is mapped to the point $(\frac{18}{6},-12)=(3,-12),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$

The point P with coordinates (−9,6) lies on the curve y=f(13x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(x)?

a
(−3,6)
b
(−27,6)
c
(−3,2)
d
(−9,2)
e
(−9,18)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since f(x)=f(3⋅(13x)), the function y=f(x) represents a compression of the function y=f(13x) by a factor of 3 parallel to the x-axis. This has the effect of dividing the x-coordinates of all points on y=f(13x) by 3.

Therefore, the point (−9,6) on f(13x) is mapped to the point ((−9)3,6)=(−3,6), and this point must lie on the graph of y=f(x).
